# Handoff §9.5's particle-absorbing merge class: jparser absorbing a preceding
# particle or fragment into the following word and matching a kana-unified
# headword that is semantically absurd. Vibrato has the boundary in every one.
#
# Regenerated from examples/boundary_diag.rs over tests/fixtures/gold.jsonl and
# tests/fixtures/gold_jmdict_subset.xml (the committed gold corpus and its
# v1 index), against corpus_staging/disagreements.jsonl -- a local, gitignored
# Phase 0 measurement artifact already present in this environment and
# byte-identical in its gold half to the committed corpus. That run reproduces
# handoff §9's headline table exactly (266 boundaries, 178/52/36 by stage,
# 92 in the "ordinary longer headword" kind). This project's own §9.5 sample
# listed ten rows out of "roughly 28" from that 92-row bucket without
# enumerating the rest; the remaining rows below were hand-classified against
# that same 92-row bucket for this task, cross-checked against each matched
# ent_seq's actual JMdict gloss (via tests/fixtures/gold_jmdict_subset.xml)
# and, where the gloss alone did not settle it, against the exact gold-span
# boundaries of the originating sentence in tests/fixtures/gold.jsonl. Two
# variant surfaces of an already-documented ent_seq (a different exact text
# hitting the same spurious match) are included alongside it. Three katakana
# homophone-collision rows (クで/タは/ヌの) and one differently-shaped row
# (的で, from 目的 mis-split) that handoff §9.5 also names are excluded here:
# they do not fit the surface/ent_seq/split shape this file uses, matching
# this task's brief, which already excludes them from its own template.
#
# The accounting is not closed. 26 rows here + the 3 excluded katakana rows +
# the 1 excluded 目的 row = 30, past the source document's own "roughly 28" --
# and a first pass at this file (task 15) missed タッとい/1598620 (added on
# review) among the 92, so the 92-row bucket may still hold rows this pass
# also missed. Treat 26 as a lower bound on the class within this file's
# shape, not a closed count.
#
# The third column is documentation, not a literal reconstruction of the
# surface: it is not checked by the test, and for some rows (はこ, どうし,
# ことし, いっしょ) it names wider sentence context or a lemma form that does
# not fit the surface's own character count. See task-15-report.md's fix
# addendum for why asserting it mechanically was judged not cheap enough to
# do here.
#
# Nothing here is captured text or ta-old expression: these are ordinary
# Japanese strings this project measured about its own engine.
#
# surface	ent_seq	what it actually is
